skill_drafts.name: Migrate Custom Observation Convention from TagProvider
skill_drafts.description: Replace deprecated TagProvider/TagContributor instrumentation with custom ServerRequestObservationConvention implementation. Reimplement custom metrics tagging using the new Observation convention pattern to preserve custom metric tags during Spring Boot 3.0 migration.
skill_drafts.objective: Reimplement custom metrics tagging using new Observation convention pattern
applicable_signals: Custom TagProvider or TagContributor classes exist in codebase
Need to preserve custom metric tags during upgrade
contraindications: No custom tags are defined in codebase
Using only default observation instrumentation without overrides
TagProvider classes are not overridden or extended
intervention_moves: Identify all custom TagProvider and TagContributor implementations
Create new class extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention or implementing ServerRequestObservationConvention
Override getLowCardinalityKeyValues() to preserve custom tags
Override getContextualName() for custom trace naming
Register custom convention bean in Spring configuration
Test that custom tags appear in metrics and traces
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Locate all custom TagProvider, TagContributor, and *Tags classes in codebase'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Create new class extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention or implementing ServerRequestObservationConvention'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Override getLowCardinalityKeyValues(ServerRequestObservationContext context) to add custom KeyValue pairs using super.getLowCardinalityKeyValues(context).and(customKeyValue)'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Override getContextualName(ServerRequestObservationContext context) to set custom trace names'}
{'step': 7, 'action': 'Remove or disable old TagProvider and TagContributor implementations'}
{'step': 8, 'action': 'Test that custom tags appear in metrics and traces with expected values'}
triggers: Custom TagProvider or TagContributor classes exist in codebase; migrating to Spring Boot 3.0; need to preserve custom metric tags
constraints: Custom convention must implement or extend ServerRequestObservationConvention interface
getContextualName() must return String for trace naming
Custom KeyValue pairs should use consistent naming conventions
cautions: Deprecated TagProvider and TagContributor classes are kept during deprecation phase but will be removed in future versions
Duplicate instrumentation risk if both old and new conventions are active; ensure old classes are removed
Custom tags must have low cardinality to avoid metric explosion
output_contract: Custom ServerRequestObservationConvention class implemented with overridden getLowCardinalityKeyValues() and getContextualName() methods; custom tags preserved and visible in metrics and traces; old TagProvider/TagContributor classes removed from active codebase

examples.input: Existing custom TagProvider that adds 'custom.method' tag to metrics
examples.output: New ExtendedServerRequestObservationConvention class extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention with getLowCardinalityKeyValues() returning super values plus KeyValue.of('custom.method', context.getCarrier().getMethod())
examples.notes: Preserves default tags while adding custom tag

examples.input: Custom TagContributor implementing full tag set
examples.output: New CustomServerRequestObservationConvention implementing ServerRequestObservationConvention with getName(), getContextualName(), and getLowCardinalityKeyValues() methods returning custom KeyValues
examples.notes: Full control over all tags; no inheritance from defaults

metadata.prompt: When you have custom TagProvider or TagContributor classes in your Spring Boot 2.x codebase, migrate them to Spring Boot 3.0 by extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention or implementing ServerRequestObservationConvention directly. Override getLowCardinalityKeyValues() to add custom KeyValue pairs, and override getContextualName() to set trace names. Preserve your custom tag logic by calling super methods and appending custom KeyValues.

skill_drafts.name: Deprecation Mapping: Spring Boot 2.x Instrumentation Classes
skill_drafts.description: Reference guide mapping deprecated instrumentation classes from Spring Boot 2.x to their Spring Boot 3.0 replacements. Covers server-side filters, client-side customizers, and tag-related classes that have been removed or superseded by Observation support.
skill_drafts.objective: Provide lookup reference for deprecated-to-replacement class mappings during Spring Boot 3.0 migration
applicable_signals: Migration from Spring Boot 2.x to 3.0 is in progress
contraindications: No deprecated instrumentation classes present in codebase
Using Spring Boot 2.x (reference is for 3.0 migration only)
triggers: Identifying which instrumentation classes need replacement
Planning migration scope for metrics and observation
Searching for equivalent functionality in Spring Boot 3.0
constraints: This is a static reference; does not execute migration logic
Functional equivalence requires understanding Observation conventions
Custom TagProvider or TagContributor implementations require extension of DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention
output_contract: Developer can quickly identify the replacement class for each deprecated instrumentation class and understand the functional shift from direct instrumentation to Observation-based conventions.

examples.output: Replace with Spring Framework's ServerHttpObservationFilter; update to use ServerRequestObservationConvention for custom behavior
Replace with ObservationRestTemplateCustomizer; apply to RestTemplateBuilder bean

examples.input: Have custom TagProvider or TagContributor implementations
examples.output: Extend DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention and override getLowCardinalityKeyValues() to add custom KeyValues

skill_drafts.name: Implement Custom ServerRequestObservationConvention
skill_drafts.description: Create a custom ServerRequestObservationConvention class by extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention or implementing the interface directly to define metric names, trace names, and low-cardinality key-value pairs for Spring Boot 3.0 observation instrumentation.
skill_drafts.objective: Code a single observation convention class with metric/trace naming and key-value extraction logic
applicable_signals: TagProvider or TagContributor classes are deprecated in Spring Boot 3.0
Observation support has replaced previous instrumentation filters
Custom tags must be migrated from legacy tag infrastructure
contraindications: Default observation behavior is sufficient and no custom metric naming is required
No custom tagging or key-value extraction is needed
Application does not use HTTP server observations
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Choose extension strategy', 'detail': 'Decide whether to extend DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention (to keep defaults and add custom tags) or implement ServerRequestObservationConvention directly (for full control).'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Override getName()', 'detail': "Return the metric name string (e.g., 'http.server.requests') that will be used for the metric name in observations."}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Override getContextualName()', 'detail': "Return a contextual name string (e.g., 'http get') that will be used for the trace name in observations."}

{'step': 4, 'action': 'Override getLowCardinalityKeyValues()', 'detail': 'Extract and return KeyValues from ServerRequestObservationContext. If extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention, call super.getLowCardinalityKeyValues(context).and(custom(context)) to augment defaults.'}

{'step': 5, 'action': 'Define custom KeyValue extraction', 'detail': 'Create helper methods (e.g., custom()) to extract specific context fields (method, status, exception) and return as KeyValue objects.'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Register as Spring bean', 'detail': 'Annotate the class with @Component or define it in a @Configuration class to ensure Spring discovers and registers it.'}
{'step': 7, 'action': 'Test and verify', 'detail': 'Deploy and verify that custom metric names, trace names, and tags appear correctly in metrics output.'}
triggers: Need to define custom metric names for HTTP server observations
Require custom trace names beyond default naming
Must add custom tags or key-value pairs to observations
constraints: Class must implement ServerRequestObservationConvention interface or extend DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention
Must be registered as a Spring bean for automatic discovery
getName() must return a valid metric name string
cautions: Ensure custom KeyValue names do not conflict with reserved observation keys
Low-cardinality keys should have bounded value sets to avoid metric explosion
Test that custom tags appear correctly in metrics output before deploying
output_contract: Compiled ServerRequestObservationConvention subclass with overridden methods; bean registered in Spring context; custom metric names, trace names, and tags appear in metrics output and traces.

examples.input: Extend DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention to add a custom 'custom.method' tag
examples.output: Class ExtendedServerRequestObservationConvention extends DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention with overridden getLowCardinalityKeyValues() that calls super and appends KeyValue.of('custom.method', context.getCarrier().getMethod())
examples.notes: Preserves all default tags while adding one custom tag

examples.input: Implement ServerRequestObservationConvention directly with full control over metric name, trace name, and tags
examples.output: Class CustomServerRequestObservationConvention implements ServerRequestObservationConvention with getName() returning 'http.server.requests', getContextualName() returning 'http ' + method, and getLowCardinalityKeyValues() returning KeyValues.of(method, status, exception)
examples.notes: Full control; no default tags inherited

metadata.prompt: Implement a ServerRequestObservationConvention by either extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention (to augment default behavior) or implementing the interface directly (for full control). Override getName() for metric name, getContextualName() for trace name, and getLowCardinalityKeyValues() to define custom tags. Register the class as a Spring bean. Verify custom tags appear in metrics output.
